correctness.rationale: Length-one overlap exclusion makes the first- and last-symbol sets disjoint. Over three symbols, reversal and relabeling can therefore always place a nonempty code among the 48 unbordered length-five words with starts in {0,2} and end 1. A checked conflict clique can meet a legal code at most once. The 28 weighted groups cover every eligible word with numerator at least 16, and their total numerator is 98, so 16|C|≤98 and |C|≤6. Independently rebuilt compatibility graphs and an exact coloring-bounded clique census confirmed the six-word witness, checked all 954 within-group pairs of the frozen certificate, and found (T_n,E_n)=(1,6),(2,18),(3,60),(6,72) at n=2,3,4,5. Comparing complete sets of codebooks under common alphabet relabeling and global reversal verified all seven listed orbit representatives and sizes 12,12,12,6,12,12,6, not just their total. A separate run without the deletion conflict confirmed 17. At length one the sole deletion descendant of every word is empty, so the first blocklength with at least four messages is indeed five. Deletion may occur at any coordinate of the identified word.
residual_risks: The census is exhaustive only for the stated finite lengths and alphabet. It does not certify streaming resynchronization after boundary-crossing corruption or after edits of more than one symbol.

evidence: Blackburn bounds pure non-overlap, and the 2024 table gives S(3,5)=17. The deletion-only maximum is 24. Non-overlap with Hamming distance at least two has maximum 9.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These give upper bounds, not the sharp 6. Single-deletion correction implies distance at least two, since a differing coordinate in a distance-one pair can be deleted from both words. The converse does not give disjoint deletion shadows, and neither of the single-constraint optima proves a sharp joint result.

evidence: The frozen six-word witness shares two-deletion descendants and includes a pair at Hamming distance two. The closest indexed records impose either two-deletion correction without overlap restrictions, or a Hamming error model.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither the matching two-deletion size nor the Hamming-model results are specializations that give the one-deletion optimum or enumeration. A two-deletion upper bound for a stricter channel is not an upper bound for one-deletion codes, and an optimum without the framing condition is not automatically a witness with it.

value.rationale: The finite cutoff has a concrete coding interpretation: length five is the smallest ternary blocklength carrying four messages with both framing and single-deletion correction. The sharp comparison 17 versus 6 isolates the cost of the added constraint at that length. The upper certificate and complete equality classification identify all optimal designs up to the natural symmetries, rather than reporting a single feasible code or recomputing the known uncorrected table.
residual_risks: These are exact short-block invariants, not a rate theorem or a decoder result for concatenated blocks.
